title: RBAC: add optimize.suggestions.read scope + enforcement for Suggestions API
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
description: Context: the new Console Suggestions view calls the Optimize Suggestions API (list + details) and must respect org/project scoping and RBAC. This PR introduces a dedicated permission scope `optimize.suggestions.read` and enforces it server-side on `/v1/optimize/suggestions` and `/v1/optimize/suggestions/{id}`. Implementation details: (1) adds the scope to the authz policy bundle and wires it into the API gateway middleware, (2) ensures suggestions queries are always constrained to the caller’s org_id + optional project_id (no cross-tenant leakage), (3) returns a consistent 403 payload (`error_code=INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS`, `required_scope=optimize.suggestions.read`) that the Console can map to the RBAC denied empty state, and (4) emits audit log events for both allow/deny decisions with minimal fields (org_id, actor_id, resource_type=optimize_suggestions, action=read, decision, request_id) to support internal access investigations (see INT-11307). Tests: adds unit tests for policy evaluation, integration tests for the API handlers (403/200), and regression coverage for org boundary enforcement. Notes: this PR does not change feature-flag gating; it only ensures that once enabled, access is still permissioned. It also does not create a write/apply permission; that will be introduced separately when we add ‘apply suggestion’ actions.
commits: authz: add optimize.suggestions.read scope to policy bundle
api: enforce optimize suggestions read permission on list + get endpoints
audit: emit authz decision events for optimize suggestions read
tests: add policy + handler integration coverage for 403 + org boundary
review_conversation: Chloe Martin (review): Can we ensure the list endpoint can’t be used to infer other orgs’ routes/models via sort keys or pagination tokens? The query should hard-filter org_id before applying sort/limit. Also please confirm we don’t log raw route names in audit logs.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Good call. Updated query builder to apply `org_id`/`project_id` predicate as the first clause before ordering/limit, and added a test asserting pagination tokens are not portable across orgs. Audit event payload now only includes `resource_type` + `action` + org_id + actor_id + decision + request_id; no route/model identifiers.

Marcus Lin (security review): Two asks: (1) Use a dedicated scope name rather than reusing optimize.read (future-proofing). (2) For denied requests, we should still emit an audit event but avoid leaking the required scope list to unprivileged callers beyond the single required scope for this endpoint.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Implemented `optimize.suggestions.read` as a dedicated scope. 403 response now includes only `required_scope=optimize.suggestions.read` and a generic message. Deny audits are emitted with the same minimal fields as allow. Added coverage for deny path emitting audit event.

Dylan Brooks (review): Console expects a stable error shape for the RBAC denied empty state. Can we align on `error_code=INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` and add `required_scope` so we can show an admin-friendly message?
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Done. Also added a short note in docs/internal/rbac/scopes.md so Support/CS can reference the scope when customers ask for access.
Jada Williams (arch): Any performance impact? This endpoint will be hit on page load for beta accounts.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Negligible; we’re reusing the existing scope evaluation path. Added a micro-benchmark note in the PR description and ensured audit emission is async/non-blocking (best-effort).
Chloe Martin (review): Approving. Please make sure integration tests run in CI; last run didn’t include the new tenancy suite.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Fixed CI target to include the new integration test file; reran CI. All green.
Marcus Lin (security review): Approved after changes.
merge_outcome: Merged to main after approvals; no rollback required
